headline: Revenue growth accelerates, margins narrow on higher costs
summary_short: Verisk's Q2 2026 revenue rose to $806.3M (+4.4% y/y, +3.0% q/q, +5.8% on an organic constant-currency basis) while net income fell to $228.6M (-9.8% y/y) on a higher tax rate, higher net interest expense, and litigation-related legal fees; diluted EPS was $1.75 (-3.3% y/y).
summary_long: Underwriting revenue grew on annual price increases and expanded sales; Claims revenue grew on anti-fraud analytics and property/restoration demand; combined OCC growth was 5.8%. Net income and diluted EPS fell y/y on a higher effective tax rate (24.6% vs 22.7%), higher net interest expense ($52.8M vs $35.5M), and litigation-related legal fees, partly offset by a lower share count; diluted adjusted (non-GAAP) EPS rose to $1.98 (+5.3% y/y). Free cash flow rose to $297.9M (+57.9% y/y). The company paid a $0.50/share dividend and executed a $200M accelerated buyback, with $800M left under authorization. Full-year 2026 guidance (revenue $3,190-3,240M, adjusted EBITDA $1,790-1,830M, diluted adjusted EPS $7.45-7.75) was reaffirmed unchanged.

drivers.explanation: Underwriting revenue grew on annual price increases from enhancements to forms/rules/loss-cost models and expanded sales to new and existing customers; Claims revenue grew on anti-fraud analytics and property/restoration solutions.
Growth is fully explained by revenue rising faster than cost of revenues (revenue +4.4% y/y vs cost of revenues +1.7% y/y), widening gross margin.

Revenue growth outpaced a rise in operating expenses (+5.8% y/y) that included $18.7M of acquisition-related fees and a $2.0M litigation reserve, both newly disclosed this quarter versus none a year ago.

Diverges from Operating income because EBIT is computed off net income plus interest/tax add-backs, which do not offset the quarter's $16.6M swing in investment results (a $7.5M loss vs a $9.1M gain a year ago) that Operating income excludes entirely.

Same mechanism as EBIT: adding back higher interest expense and a flat tax provision does not offset the net-income decline driven by the investment-result swing and litigation/tax items, so unadjusted EBITDA still falls even as revenue and operating income rise.
Decline was mainly driven by a higher effective tax rate, higher net interest expense, and legal fees tied to ongoing litigation.
Fell on higher net interest expense, a higher effective tax rate, and increased litigation-related legal fees, partly offset by a lower average diluted share count and operational performance.

Management framed the quarter as a sequential acceleration toward Investor Day targets, citing 8.0% underlying subscription growth and continued AI investment, and reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance unchanged.
